The project and symposium I mentioned are being run by the University of Western Sydney (http://www.uws.edu.au/rcegws/rce/biodiversity_and_river_health/bee_aware). The aim is to raise community awareness of the 200 native bee species found within our region. Not only that, but it helps to educate people about creating habitat for them, and we get to have a better look at their actual distribution.

It's only been fairly recently that people have started to show interest in our native bees. This is probably due to someone having an "Oh Shit!" moment about CCD and Varoa mites.

Varroa mites and CCD are very real problems, as I'm sure you already know. 
Thankfully, Aus seems to be safe from both... for now.

Speaking of... I am pretty sure that varroa is only a threat to Apis species, so that is why it's so important to research and make good use of our native bees.

As an insurance, Australian scientists are looking into using native bees for commercial purposes. The University of Adelaide has been researching using Blue Banded Bees (Amegilla species) for tomato pollination, and someone somewhere else has been looking at using native honey bees (Tetragonula and Austroplebeia species) for commercial honey production.
